title: Sikh Empire history - rise, peak and fall of Punjab's golden age
hook: What if a modest warrior band transformed Punjab from a crumbling Mughal fringe into a mighty empire that stunned the British?
description:
Explore the rise, peak, and fall of the Sikh Empire-how a regional power reshaped South Asia in just five decades.

beats.say: In 1700 Punjab splinters under weakened Mughal rule, while autonomous Sikh bands begin organizing their own territories.
By 1800 Maharaja Ranjit Singh unites the bands, declares Lahore his capital, and launches the Sikh Empire.
In 1805 his forces capture Amritsar, securing the spiritual heart of Sikhism and consolidating power.
The 1815 victory at the Battle of Multan drives the Afghans back, expanding the empire to the Khyber Pass.
By 1820 Ranjit crowns himself Maharaja, annexes Kashmir, and controls the Himalayas from Kashmir to the Khyber.
In 1829 the empire reaches its zenith, boasting a modernized army, navy on the Indus, and thriving trade.
The 1845 First Anglo-Sikh War shatters the balance, forcing Ranjit's heirs into costly peace.
By 1849 after the Second Anglo-Sikh War, the British annex Punjab, ending sovereign rule forever.
Surprisingly, the Sikh Empire's brief existence forged a legacy of secular governance that still shapes Indian Punjab today.
